title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 345 (Books and papers of company to be evidence)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up, all books and papers of the company and of the Company Liquidator shall, as between the contributories of the company, be prima facie evidence of the truth of all matters purporting to be recorded therein.
content.glance: Company and Liquidator books/papers are prima facie evidence as between contributories of matters recorded in them.
content.study: Section 345 creates a statutory prima facie evidentiary rule. In a winding up, the books and papers of the company and of the Company Liquidator are, as between the contributories, prima facie evidence of the truth of all matters purporting to be recorded in them. The rule facilitates proof of accounts, shareholdings and other recorded facts among contributories without requiring formal proof of every entry, while remaining open to rebuttal.

sections.heading: Prima facie evidence
sections.body: Books and papers of the company and of the Company Liquidator are prima facie evidence as between contributories of the truth of recorded matters.

provisions.title: Books and papers of company to be evidence

examples.title: Share register entry
examples.body: In a dispute among contributories over the number of shares held, the company’s register is relied on under s. 345 as prima facie evidence of the recorded holding.

hypotheticals.question: Is the evidentiary rule conclusive?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is only prima facie evidence and may be rebutted by contrary proof.

rows.left: Books and papers of company to be evidence

misconceptions.trap: Books are conclusive evidence against all persons.
misconceptions.correction: The rule applies as between the contributories and is only prima facie, not conclusive.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 345 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the rule of s. 345. II. Apply to facts. III. Conclude.
